Subject: Weekly MAP checkpoint: HelioHealth private capacity sizing & evaluation timeline

Hi Alice / Matt —

Thanks again for taking time last week. Per our MAP, attaching an updated Mutual Action Plan workbook (Helio_MAP_v3.xlsx) with the evaluation milestones and a first-pass sizing worksheet. This thread will be our weekly checkpoint for capacity and timeline items. Summary items below: 

- Goal: Private deployment (VPC) for model serving by end of Q2; full evaluation and go/no-go decision by 2026-06-30.
- Immediate ask this week: confirm preferred GPU type (H100 vs A100 tradeoff), target steady-state throughput and peak burst profile, and primary regions (we propose us-west-2 + us-east-1 + eu-west-1).
- Perf targets provided by Helio: 95th percentile latency <200ms for single-request chat flows; single-request token throughput TBD.

Proposed sizing windows (high-level):
- Option A (performance-first): H100 devices, 3 regions, 4 GPUs per region (12 H100 total) — expected to meet 95th <200ms and handle ~12k tokens/sec steady across regions with 2x burst headroom.
- Option B (cost-optimized): A100 80GB, 3 regions, 8 GPUs per region (24 A100 total) with aggressive quantization and batching — similar throughput but higher latency tail risk.

Action items (owners):
- AI-01: Helio to confirm throughput (steady/peak) and region priorities — Alice / Matt (due: 2026-03-04)
- RD-01: Redwood to produce a short perf-run plan (bench scripts, dataset, target metrics) — Dev Patel (due: 2026-03-06)
- OPS-01: Provision staging cluster spec for soak tests — Sergio Alvarez (due: 2026-03-09)
- PROC-01: Procurement kickoff (SOW/PO checklist + timeline) — Lauren Bishop (due: 2026-03-10)

Attachments: Helio_MAP_v3.xlsx (MAP workbook, milestones), gpu_sizing_matrix.pdf (detailed sizing options).

Can we confirm a 30-minute check on Wednesday 03/04 10:00 PT? If that works we’ll send an invite and include the staging runbook.

Thanks —
Nikhil

Appreciate the clear summary and the workbook. Quick answers from our side: 

- Regions: confirmed — priority is us-west-2 (primary), us-east-1 (failover), and eu-west-1 (GDPR/aligned).
- Throughput targets: steady-state target across product should be ~6,000 tokens/sec (aggregate user traffic) with anticipated peak bursts up to 12,000 tokens/sec for sustained 5-minute windows during batch runs. We also want per-request latencies: 95th <200ms as you noted.
- GPU preference: we prefer H100 if cost delta is acceptable; our finance lead wants a clear TCO comparison vs A100 including expected pre-quantization token cost.

Procurement is looped in (procure@heliohealth.com) — they’ll need a high-level BOM and estimated monthly committed hours for Dedicated/Private.

Wednesday 03/04 10:00 PT works for a 30-minute checkpoint. Please include your perf-run plan and a preliminary cost delta table in the invite.

Best,

Subject: Re: Weekly MAP checkpoint: HelioHealth private capacity sizing & evaluation timeline

Thanks Alice — good clarity on steady vs peak. Based on those numbers, preliminary sizing and test plan below. Attaching the GPU sizing matrix as a reference.

Prelim sizing (expected to meet 6k steady / 12k short-burst across 3 regions):
- H100 path (recommended for latency-sensitive workloads): 4x H100 per region (us-west-2, us-east-1, eu-west-1) = 12 H100 total. Expected steady throughput ~6k tokens/sec with 2x headroom for short bursts; 95p latency projected <200ms with optimized kernels + KV cache.
- A100 path (cost-first): 8x A100 80GB per region = 24 A100 total. Achieves similar aggregate throughput with more aggressive batching and quantization; expect higher 95p latency risk (200-300ms) and more manual tuning.

Notes on autoscaling and capacity management:
- Autoscale policy: maintain a hot pool sized for steady-state + 30% buffer, allow burst autoscale (up to 2x) with ephemeral preemption policy.
- Caching: prefix + KV cache will lower per-token cost for chat scenarios; include benchmark sets that mirror Helio’s prod prompt shapes.

Proposed perf evaluation plan (Dev / Sergio owner split):
- Phase 1 (Perf bench): run controlled load tests against model variants (float32, q8_0, q4f16) to measure tokens/sec, p95 latency, and memory footprint. (Owner: Dev; due: 2026-03-10)
- Phase 2 (Soak + Failover): 24h soak in staging across 3 regions with normal traffic mix + simulated failover. (Owner: Sergio; due: 2026-03-16)
- Phase 3 (Cost projection): use run outputs to produce a monthly committed-hours TCO and per-token cost for H100 vs A100. (Owner: Lauren; due: 2026-03-18)

Action items updates (from Nikhil’s MAP):
- RD-01: Redwood perf-run plan — Dev Patel (2026-03-06) [updating to 2026-03-10 after initial bench creation]
- OPS-01: Staging cluster provisioning — Sergio Alvarez (2026-03-09)
- PROC-01: Procurement SOW checklist — Lauren Bishop (2026-03-10)

Open question for Helio: do you have a preferred model family we should focus on for the bench (open-model LlamaX v2 / Mistral / customer-provided)? This will affect memory and batching assumptions.

Thanks —
Dev Patel
Senior SRE, Redwood Inference
